answers.explanation: 172.20 is inside 172.16 to 172.31. 172.32 is just outside it, and 192.169 isn't 192.168.
RFC 1918 addresses are non-routable: many networks use the same ones, so the Internet drops them.
127.0.0.1, also known as localhost. The whole 127 network is reserved for loopback.
Loopback never touches the cable or the NIC. If it fails, look at the host itself.
The NAT router sits between the two networks and rewrites addresses as packets cross.
It tracks each connection by port number, so replies get back to the right host.
169.254 is link-local. It's the classic sign that DHCP failed.
128 is an ordinary class B range. The three private ranges are the other three.
